Day 2 Convective Outlook CORR 1
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0708 AM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 121200Z - 131200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
CENTRAL AND NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS...AND ALSO FOR PARTS OF THE MIDWEST
AND OHIO VALLEY...

CORRECTED FOR REVERSED THUNDER LINE IN SOUTH-CENTRAL US

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe gusts and hail will be possible Wednesday
afternoon and evening across parts of the central and northern High
Plains. Damaging gusts and isolated hail will also be possible
across parts of the Midwest and Ohio Valley.

...Parts of the Midwest/Ohio Valley...
Guidance continues to vary considerably regarding potential for
early-day convection across parts of the Midwest and Ohio Valley.
Any morning convection will in turn influence the position of an
effective frontal zone that will generally extend from parts of the
mid MO Valley into the lower OH Valley. Strong heating, rich
low-level moisture, and generally steep lapse rates will result in
strong to extreme buoyancy to the warm side of the front, with
substantial MUCAPE possible to the immediate cool side of the front.


Multiple scenarios are possible. There will be some potential for
any early-day storm cluster to propagate southeastward through the
day, with a damaging-wind and isolated hail threat. Diurnal
development will be possible in the vicinity of the frontal zone,
with sufficient deep-layer shear for initial supercell potential.
Hail and possibly a tornado could accompany the strongest diurnal
storms, though there may be a tendency for clustering and perhaps
organized upscale growth, with increasing wind-damage potential.
While uncertainty remains high, one or more rounds of
organized-severe potential could evolve in the vicinity of the
frontal zone, and a 15% wind area was added where guidance currently
has the greatest signal for development. 
 
...Parts of the central/northern High Plains into the lower/mid
Missouri Valley...
To the north of a surface low across southeast CO and an
eastward-extending warm front, moist low-level easterly flow will
support potential for moderate to locally strong destabilization
across parts of western SD/NE into northwest KS/far northeast CO.
Midlevel flow will be relatively modest, but veering wind profiles
will result in sufficient deep-layer shear for storm organization.

Initial isolated to widely scattered discrete development could pose
a threat of hail and localized severe gusts. Some upscale growth and
possible MCS development may occur during the late evening and
overnight across parts of central/eastern NE and vicinity. Guidance
varies regarding the organization of any nocturnal MCS, but at least
isolated damaging-wind potential could spread eastward through the
end of the period.  

...Northern SD/southern ND into parts of MN/WI/MI...
While the strongest instability will remain south of the region,
moderate buoyancy is forecast to develop along/ahead of a front
draped from near the ND/SD border into southern MN, WI, and Lower
MI. Coverage of storms is uncertain within this regime, but moderate
northwesterly mid/upper-level flow and favorable deep-layer shear
will support organized convection, with a threat for strong to
locally severe gusts and hail if any sustained storms develop. 

...Carolinas/Southern Appalachians...
The evolution of antecedent upstream convection will have a
considerable influence on the position of the primary surface front
and any organized severe threat across parts of the southern
Appalachians and Carolinas region on Wednesday. At least isolated
storm development will be possible near the front and also across
favored terrain areas, with modest west-northwesterly flow aloft
supporting potential for outflow-driven cells/clusters with a threat
of wind damage. Any features favorably timed with the diurnal cycle
(such as a persistent storm cluster or MCV) could result in a
greater coverage of wind-damage potential, but confidence in the
details is too low for more than 5% wind probabilities at this time.

..Dean.. 08/11/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0230 AM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 131200Z - 141200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE CENTRAL
HIGH PLAINS INTO THE OHIO VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms are possible on Thursday from the central
High Plains into the Ohio Valley.

...Central High Plains eastward to the Ohio Valley...
Elevated convection and possibly a remnant MCS may be ongoing at the
start of the forecast period across parts of IA/northern MO into IL,
aided by a southwesterly low-level jet. Large-scale support for this
convection is generally forecast to weaken through the day, though
any remnant storm cluster or MCV may become the focus for afternoon
intensification and wind-damage potential into parts of the Ohio
Valley, if it is well-timed with downstream diurnal destabilization.

Otherwise, moderate to strong destabilization will again be possible
from parts of the Midwest into the central Plains, in the vicinity
of a frontal zone. The position of the frontal zone is uncertain due
to the influence of antecedent Day 1-2 convection, and large-scale
ascent appears nebulous at best for much of the day within a regime
of weak midlevel height rises. Isolated storm development cannot be
ruled out near the front through early evening, with somewhat
greater coverage possible across parts of the central High Plains
and adjacent higher terrain. Low-level warm advection may allow for
an increase in storm coverage into late evening near the front,
though the later activity would likely be somewhat elevated.  

Deep-layer shear will generally be somewhat weaker than previous
days, but still sufficient for some storm organization where deep
convection can be sustained. A broad 5% area has been included in
the anticipated vicinity of the frontal zone, though confidence in
the details of storm development and evolution remains rather low. 

...Parts of the Great Lakes and Northeast...
Moderate to strong west-northwesterly mid/upper-level flow will
overspread parts of the Great Lakes and Northeast on Thursday, in
association with a seasonably deep upper trough extending from
eastern Canada into the northeast CONUS. Guidance varies
considerably regarding the extent (if any) of destabilization across
this region during the afternoon. Probabilities may eventually be
needed for parts of this region, if confidence increases regarding
sufficient destabilization in association with the strengthening
wind fields.

..Dean.. 08/11/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0313 AM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 141200Z - 191200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...D4/Friday...
Moderate to strong destabilization will again be possible on Friday,
near and south of a front extending from the central Plains and
Midwest into parts of the southern Mid-Atlantic. Considerable
uncertainty remains regarding the exact frontal position, but strong
storms will be possible in its vicinity. Most guidance depicts
rising midlevel heights and modest deep-layer flow/shear in the
vicinity of the frontal zone, which may tend to keep the severe
threat isolated. One possible exception will be in the Carolinas and
southern VA, where the glancing influence of a seasonably deep upper
trough over the Northeast may result in a somewhat more organized
severe threat, if sufficient destabilization can occur.  

...D5/Saturday - D6/Sunday...
Some dampening of the upper ridge (potentially aided by one or more
MCVs emerging from the High Plains) may result in severe potential
emerging this weekend across parts of the Upper Midwest and Great
Lakes/Ohio Valley. However, details regarding timing of any
shortwave troughs and position of the primary frontal zone remain
quite uncertain. 

...D7/Monday - D8/Tuesday...
Extended-range guidance generally suggests potential for a
northwesterly flow regime to develop from the northern Plains into
parts of the East by early next week. Predictability remains quite
low regarding the extent to which stronger deep-layer flow impinges
upon favorable instability, but at least isolated severe potential
may eventually develop from parts of the north-central CONUS into
the Mid-Atlantic and Carolinas.

..Dean.. 08/11/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1200 AM CDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM NORTHERN
ILLINOIS INTO THE OHIO VALLEY...

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF THE
NORTHERN PLAINS...AND FROM IOWA TO VIRGINIA...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts will be possible today
from the eastern Iowa/northern Illinois vicinity into parts of the
Ohio Valley and central Appalachians. Areas of severe wind gusts and
hail will also be possible over parts of the northern Plains.

...IA to the Mid-Atlantic...

A complex forecast scenario is expected today from IA into the Ohio
Valley and adjacent Appalachia. More than one MCS may be ongoing at
the beginning of the period. The first across IA/southern MN, and
one further southeast across parts of the Midwest (exact location is
uncertain, but most likely IN/OH). Possible early day convection
across IN/OH will spread east/southeast across the Ohio Valley
during the morning posing risk for strong gusts. This activity is
likely to emerge across Appalachia, and eventually VA and the
broader Mid-Atlantic during the afternoon/evening. How much
destabilization will occur across VA and the Mid-Atlantic remains
uncertain given prior convection the previous day and potential
convective debris across the region. Some damaging wind potential
could materialize if sufficient destabilization occurs during the
afternoon.

The anticipated MCS over IA/southern MN early in the forecast period
is then expected to continue east/southeast across the Midwest,
fueled by a very moist and strongly unstable boundary layer.
Midlevel flow is forecast to be quite strong (by August standards),
with forecast guidance suggesting 700 mb greater than 60 kt
spreading across the Midwest through evening. While the exact
evolution of a potential severe MCS moving across the Midwest is
uncertain, it is possible the morning activity over IA will develop
southeast along outflow across the Ohio Valley. Given the strong
kinematic field and ample instability, if a well organized MCS is
maintained from IA southeast into the OH Valley, a swath of damaging
gusts (some 75+ mph) will be possible.

...Northern Plains...

East/southeasterly flow along the surface trough is forecast to
maintain 60s F dewpoints across the western Dakotas and parts of NE
this afternoon. Steep midlevel lapse rates atop the relatively moist
boundary layer, and strong heating will support a corridor of
moderate to strong instability across the western Dakotas. Scattered
storms are expected by early evening amid supercell wind profiles.
Elongated hodographs favorable for splitting cells with an
accompanying risk for large to very large hail are forecast.
Isolated severe gusts also could occur. Given a lack of stronger
low-level jet during the nighttime hours, it appears unlikely that
upscale growth will occur, and convection is expected to wane with
eastward extent overnight.

..Leitman/Moore.. 08/11/2026
